title: A virtual measurement bench
purpose: Bring algebra, function interpretation, trigonometry, and matrix methods together in six small investigations using supplied idealized data. No hardware purchase or prior circuit theory is needed.
effort: Approximately 3 to 5 focused hours with saved progress between tasks.
deliverable: A structured notebook containing definitions, equations, calculations, domain and unit checks, graph/table comparisons, and short explanations. Export a readable report with the submitted values and rubric state.

tasks.title: Calibrate a sensor
tasks.given: A temperature sensor produces 0.5 V at 0 degrees C and 2.5 V at 100 degrees C. Assume a linear response within that calibration interval.
tasks.work: Define variables and units; derive V(T) and its inverse; convert a 1.7 V reading; compare a predicted reading at 60 degrees C with an observed 1.72 V; explain whether 3.1 V is interpolation or extrapolation.
tasks.reference: V(T)=0.02*T+0.5; T(V)=(V-0.5)/0.02; 1.7 V maps to 60 degrees C. Observed-minus-predicted residual at 60 degrees C is +0.02 V. A 3.1 V reading lies outside the calibrated voltage interval.
tasks.acceptance: Both functions and units are correct, their valid modeling interval is stated, the residual sign matches its definition, and extrapolation is identified.

tasks.title: Audit a mathematical transformation
tasks.given: A synthetic error model uses p(x)=(x+2)*(x-1)^2 on [-3,3]. A separate processing rule uses q(x)=(x^2-1)/(x-1). The variable x is dimensionless.
tasks.work: Find p's zeros and multiplicities, explain crossing versus touching, simplify q, identify the input that remains invalid, and produce a table near that input.
tasks.reference: p has roots -2 with multiplicity 1 and 1 with multiplicity 2. q agrees with x+1 for x!=1 and has a hole at (1,2). q(0.9)=1.9 and q(1.1)=2.1, but q(1) is undefined.
tasks.acceptance: A smooth-looking plot must not restore the excluded input. The explanation connects factor multiplicity with behavior on both sides of each zero.

tasks.title: Estimate a decay threshold
tasks.given: A supplied idealized model is V(t)=8*exp(-t/2), with voltage in volts and time in seconds, for t>=0.
tasks.work: Interpret the initial value and decay behavior; derive the time when the signal reaches 2 V; provide an exact and a rounded value; verify by substitution; explain why reaching exactly 0 V has no finite solution in this model.
tasks.reference: The threshold time is 2*ln(4), approximately 2.772588722 s. The exponent uses a 2-second time constant. V remains positive for every finite nonnegative time.
tasks.acceptance: The logarithm argument is positive and dimensionless, the time is nonnegative, and the learner distinguishes an asymptotic approach from a finite zero.

tasks.title: Describe and solve a periodic signal
tasks.given: A voltage signal is v(t)=3*sin(4*pi*(t-0.125))+1, with t in seconds. Consider 0<=t<0.5.
tasks.work: Report amplitude, offset, period, frequency, and time shift; predict the peak; solve v(t)=2.5 V on the stated interval; compare a graph and an exact phase-angle calculation.
tasks.reference: Amplitude 3 V, offset 1 V, period 0.5 s, frequency 2 Hz, right shift 0.125 s. A peak occurs at t=0.25 s with 4 V. The threshold times are t=1/6 s and t=1/3 s.
tasks.acceptance: Both threshold times are present and verified, time and angle units stay distinct, and an equivalent sinusoidal representation is accepted.

tasks.title: Solve a coupled calibration
tasks.given: Two dimensionless unknown calibration parameters satisfy 2*x+y=7 and x-y=2. Compare with the altered information x+y=2 and 2*x+2*y=5.
tasks.work: Write A*x=b; solve the first system by elimination and one matrix method; compute the residual; classify the altered system; explain why an inverse does not exist for its coefficient matrix.
tasks.reference: The first system gives (3,1), determinant -3, and zero residual. The altered coefficient matrix is singular, and its augmented system is inconsistent.
tasks.acceptance: Variable order is consistent, the matrix method agrees with elimination, and singularity is distinguished from inconsistency of the augmented system.

tasks.title: Explain limits and reproduce a result
tasks.given: Use the assumptions and outputs from p01 through p05.
tasks.work: Choose one result and reproduce it with a second method. Identify one domain restriction, one measurement or rounding limitation, and one observation that would call a model into question. Summarize the distinction between supplied idealized models and measured physical behavior.
tasks.reference: Accept multiple sound explanations. Examples include an out-of-range calibration input, nonzero sensor residuals, a decay curve that stops matching observations, or inconsistent calibration equations.
tasks.acceptance: Use a transparent rubric with self-review or a human reviewer. Free-form explanations must not receive a fabricated automatic correctness score.

rubric.evidence: Variables, units, intervals, and supplied assumptions are explicit before solving.
Required numeric, symbolic, interval, and matrix outputs pass their reviewed checks.
Substitution, residuals, graph/table comparisons, and an independent method support the results.
The learner explains exclusions, full solution sets, model range, and singularity correctly.
The notebook includes enough steps and labels for another learner to follow the work.

completion: Require all structured checks and a completed rubric self-review with at least 80/100 and no missing criterion. Label the rubric score self-assessed unless an identified human reviewer supplies it. Return incomplete or invalid mathematical work for revision; allow unlimited revisions.
reviewScale: For each rubric criterion use 0 for missing, 0.5 for partially evidenced, and 1 for complete evidence, multiplied by that criterion's weight. A self-assessment records reflection, not independent certification.
variants: After the reference project is reviewed, create at least two equivalent data sets with independently verified answers. Preserve the same objectives and workload; do not simply change every number without rechecking restrictions and threshold counts.
